title: India's Biggest Trade Deal Goes Live on Tuesday. Here's What Changes for the Diaspora in Britain.
excerpt: The India-UK free trade agreement enters force on July 15, cutting tariffs to near zero on 99 per cent of Indian exports, eliminating dual social security payments for 75,000 professionals, and creating mobility pathways for IT workers, chefs and musicians.
body:
On Tuesday, the largest trade deal the United Kingdom has signed since it left the European Union will come into force. For the 1.9 million people of Indian origin living in Britain, and for the millions more who export, invest and travel between the two countries, the India-UK Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement is about to change the arithmetic of their daily and professional lives.

Signed in July 2025, the agreement was fast-tracked through both parliaments and is now days from implementation. Commerce Minister Piyush Goyal, who was in London last month finalising preparations, called it "the most comprehensive agreement India has entered into so far." British officials described it as the fastest-implemented trade pact in British parliamentary history.

## What the Deal Does

The numbers are striking. Nearly 99 per cent of Indian exports to the UK will receive duty-free or preferentially reduced access. Import duties on Indian textiles, leather goods, footwear, marine products, processed foods and engineering goods — sectors that collectively employ tens of millions of workers — will drop to zero or near zero.

On the British side, whisky tariffs fall from 150 per cent to 40 per cent. Import duties on cars entering India from the UK drop from roughly 110 per cent to 10 per cent under a quota system. India has agreed to allow 378,000 UK-origin passenger cars over the first fifteen years.

But the agreement is far more than a tariff schedule. It spans 30 chapters covering digital trade, telecommunications, financial services, intellectual property, innovation, sustainability, small and medium enterprises, government procurement, and transparency.

## The Social Security Breakthrough

Perhaps the single most consequential provision for the Indian diaspora in Britain is the Double Contribution Convention, which also takes effect on July 15. Under current rules, Indian professionals posted to the UK pay social security contributions to both countries simultaneously — a double tax that reduces take-home pay and creates administrative headaches for employers.

The convention eliminates this duplication. Indian workers posted to the UK will be exempt from British National Insurance contributions for up to five years, paying only into the Indian system. UK officials estimate the provision will benefit more than 75,000 Indian professionals and over 900 Indian companies operating in Britain.

For the thousands of IT professionals, consultants and financial services workers who rotate between Bengaluru, Pune, Hyderabad and London, the effect is immediate: higher take-home pay from the moment the convention enters force.

## A Professional Mobility Framework

The agreement creates structured mobility pathways for business visitors, intra-company transferees, contractual service suppliers, independent professionals and investors. In a provision that drew attention from diaspora cultural organisations, 1,800 Indian chefs, yoga instructors and classical musicians will receive dedicated mobility routes to work in the United Kingdom each year.

The services framework covers IT, financial services, healthcare, education, engineering and consultancy — sectors where India's workforce has strong demand from UK employers.

## Why It Matters Beyond Trade

India has been accelerating its trade diplomacy. The UK deal arrives alongside ongoing negotiations with the United States, where a separate interim trade agreement is racing against a July 24 tariff deadline, and amid a broader strategy to diversify export markets away from dependence on any single partner.

The State Bank of India's research arm described the UK agreement as signalling "a new global trade strategy" that reduces China dependence and navigates around U.S. tariff pressures. By locking in preferential access to a $3.5 trillion economy and former colonial power turned strategic partner, India gains both a commercial advantage and a diplomatic hedge.

For the UK, which has been seeking post-Brexit trade deals to justify its departure from the European Union, the India pact is politically significant. Prime Minister Keir Starmer's government has framed it as evidence that Britain can secure meaningful agreements on its own terms. "The biggest deal we've struck since we left the EU," Starmer said in a statement.

## The Steel Wrinkle

The road to July 15 was not entirely smooth. Indian officials raised concerns about new UK steel trade measures due to take effect on July 1, and there was brief speculation that New Delhi might delay or reopen the FTA. The dispute was resolved after talks between Modi and Starmer at a G7 summit in France. Approximately 85 per cent of India's steel exports to the UK remain outside the scope of the new measures, with additional safeguards built into the framework through quotas and authorised-use arrangements.

## The Diaspora as Bridge

Minister Goyal's London visit included a meeting with the Indian diaspora and business community, where he described the community as "a living bridge between India and the United Kingdom, strengthening economic, cultural, and people-to-people ties."

That bridge is about to become a highway. When the tariff reductions, the social security exemption and the mobility provisions all take effect on Tuesday, the 1.9 million Indians in Britain — and the industries that depend on the flow of goods, services and people between the two countries — will feel the difference in pounds and rupees, starting immediately.
